about: ANSI B4.1-1967 (R1999/R2004 reaffirmations) preferred limits and fits for cylindrical parts, inch. Values in thousandths of an inch (0.001 in) as printed. Each row: [limit_a, limit_b, hole_plus, hole_minus, shaft_plus, shaft_minus]. limit_a/limit_b are the two printed 'limits of clearance' (RC, LC: min, max clearance; LT: printed with minus = interference, then max clearance) or 'limits of interference' (LN, FN: min, max interference). Transcribed with the WebFetch tool (text extraction of the PDF); see notes for placement corrections.

KSU.publisher: King Saud University (faculty course material, fac.ksu.edu.sa)
KSU.title: Fits US tables, ANSI B4.1-1967 (R1987), Tables 3 to 9 (RC1-RC9, LC1-LC11, LT1-LT6, LN1-LN3, FN1-FN5), 0 to 19.69 in
KSU.note: Course reprint of the standard's tables. Text extraction loses blank cells: for 0 to 0.24 in (LT3, LT4 blank) and 0 to 0.95 in (FN3 blank) the extracted values were first placed one class too far left; BenchMate put them back in the class whose hole and shaft grades they fit (LT5 = H7/n6, LT6 = H7/n7, FN4 = H7/u6; tolerance of each limit pair equals that grade's tolerance in the same size range). Rows that do not add up as transcribed are kept as transcribed and flagged by the build.

EE.title: Standard Preferred Tolerance Limits Fits ANSI B4.1 (worked RC5 example, 2 in nominal)
EE.note: Prints one worked example only: RC5 at 2 in: hole 2.0000/2.0018, shaft 1.9963/1.9975, clearance 0.0025 to 0.0055. Its fit calculators compute on the server and could not be read.

AMES.title: ANSI preferred tolerances and fits charts (fit descriptions and hole-shaft symbols)
AMES.note: Prints the descriptions and the ISO-style symbols of each class (no limit values). No shaft symbol in the standard for RC9, LC10, LC11 and FN1.

AMES.RC1: Close sliding: accurate location of parts that must assemble without perceptible play.
AMES.RC2: Sliding: accurate location, more clearance than RC1; parts move and turn easily but are not meant to run freely; larger sizes may seize with small temperature changes.
AMES.RC3: Precision running: closest fit expected to run freely; precision work at slow speed and light journal pressure; not where appreciable temperature differences are likely.
AMES.RC4: Close running: running fits on accurate machinery with moderate surface speed and journal pressure, where accurate location and minimum play are wanted.
AMES.RC5: Medium running: higher running speeds or heavy journal pressures.
AMES.RC6: Medium running: higher running speeds or heavy journal pressures.
AMES.RC7: Free running: where accuracy is not essential, or large temperature variations are likely, or both.
AMES.RC8: Loose running: wide commercial tolerances with an allowance on the external member.
AMES.RC9: Loose running: wide commercial tolerances with an allowance on the external member.
AMES.FN1: Light drive: light assembly pressure, more or less permanent assemblies; thin sections, long fits, cast-iron external members.
AMES.FN2: Medium drive: ordinary steel parts or shrink fits on light sections; about the tightest usable with high-grade cast-iron external members.
AMES.FN3: Heavy drive: heavier steel parts or shrink fits in medium sections.
AMES.FN4: Force: parts that can be highly stressed, or shrink fits where the heavy pressing forces needed are impractical.
AMES.FN5: Force: parts that can be highly stressed, or shrink fits where the heavy pressing forces needed are impractical.
